question:
Select the most appropriate meaning of the given idiom.

To crow over something
solution:
The correct answer is "**To revel boastfully over something**."

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

 
• **The idiom "to crow over something" means to boast or brag about something in a celebratory manner.**
 
• किसी बात का उत्सवपूर्वक बखान करना या डींगें हांकना।
 
• The word "crow" in this context refers to the loud and proud cawing sound made by a rooster, which is often associated with victory and dominance.
 
• This idiom is commonly used when someone is gloating or showing off about an achievement or success.
 
 
• Example: After winning the championship game, the team captain couldn't help but crow over their victory to anyone who would listen.
 
 
 
• Thus, it is clear that option 2 explains the given idiom perfectly.

Hence, **the correct answer is option 2**.
